research.job_description_summary: Cognizant's official GenC page describes Generation Cognizant as its hiring and development programme for entry-level talent in India, with campus and off-campus drives, assessments that test communication, aptitude and/or technical skills depending on the role, interviews, and no service bond. The page names no job titles, tracks or eligibility criteria. Secondary sources describe GenC, GenC Next and GenC Elevate tracks assigned by assessment score.
limitations: The official GenC page lists the process in general terms only; it names no roles, tracks, eligibility, assessment patterns or cutoffs. The GenC Next and GenC Elevate track names and pay bands come from secondary sources (JobRise 2026-02-11, unsourced cutoffs).

The only candidate-attributed material found is two short accounts in a 2023 article (updated 2024) on placementpreparation.io, which are generic about rounds and name no specific questions beyond SQL basics and joins; those items are marked low confidence.
The JobRise guide says it spoke with 30+ candidates but does not attribute its lists of most-asked questions to individuals, so those lists were used only as topic context (class D).
A second placementpreparation.io page is partly behind a login wall; its visible sample problems are editorial and not candidate-attributed.
That page's meta description mentions another company, suggesting a copy error; its cluster descriptions (Java/SQL/web and SQL/Python/cloud) are unconfirmed.
Aptitude, communication and debugging items are original practice items.
Because the track names are secondary-sourced, track-specific question allocation is a proposed structure, not documented.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: Pipe A fills an empty tank in 10 hours and pipe B empties a full tank in 15 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?
questions.relevance_to_role: Cognizant's official GenC page says assessments test communication, aptitude and/or technical skills depending on the role.
questions.expected_answer: 30 hours
follow_ups: What if B emptied the tank in 8 hours?
questions.notes: Original practice item; the official page names the assessment areas only.

mcq.explanation: Net rate = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30 of the tank per hour, so it takes 30 hours.

questions.prompt: Given Employee(id, name, dept_id) and Department(id, name), write a query to list each employee's name with the department name.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between final, finally and finalize in Java?
questions.relevance_to_role: These keywords are listed in a 2026 Cognizant guide's most-asked list.
questions.expected_answer: final is a modifier (constant variable, non-overridable method, non-extendable class); finally is a block that runs after try/catch for cleanup; finalize() is a deprecated method called by the garbage collector before reclaiming an object.
follow_ups: Does finally run after return?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an array and an ArrayList in Java?
questions.relevance_to_role: Array versus ArrayList is listed in a 2026 Cognizant guide.
questions.expected_answer: Arrays are fixed-size, can hold primitives and are typed at creation. ArrayList is a resizable class holding objects, offering methods like add and remove, with automatic growth.
follow_ups: How does an ArrayList grow?
common_mistakes: Saying arrays are always faster in every case
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between == and equals() in Java for strings?
questions.relevance_to_role: == versus equals() is listed in a 2026 Cognizant guide.
questions.expected_answer: == compares references (same object); equals() compares content. Two strings with the same text can be different objects, so use equals() for content.
follow_ups: What does new String("hi") == "hi" give?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface?
questions.relevance_to_role: OOP principles are listed as a core interview topic in a 2026 Cognizant guide.
questions.expected_answer: An abstract class can hold state, constructors and concrete methods and supports single inheritance; an interface defines a contract (with default methods in modern Java) and a class can implement many. Use abstract classes for shared code and interfaces for capabilities.
follow_ups: Can an interface have a constructor?
common_mistakes: Saying interfaces cannot have any implementation in modern Java
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial list that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://jobrise.io/en/blog/cognizant-interview-questions-freshers-2026/.
